# Customer Loyalty and Rewards Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Customer Loyalty and Rewards Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 6 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment and maker access; confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available and keep the build Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review policies for uploaded loyalty files, the proposed ledger and CRM sources and the channel; document blocked paths instead of bypassing them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who may build, test and use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the read-only loyalty ledger, the consented CRM preference feed and the authorized rewards workflow; the workshop needs no connection. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare program, CRM, marketing and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer. | Customer or partner |
| Write-control ownership | Name who authorizes, approves and audits any future rewards action; the template performs no writes. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Loyalty program owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Program engagement, point liability, reward relevance and tier movement by tier. Agree the current shared program view before attributing any change to the adapted agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Tier | Measurement period | Active members | Points outstanding | Redemptions | Reporting effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree data sources, consent, write controls, governance, support, telemetry and success measures.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Loyalty program owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Loyalty program owner | Approve scope, data sources, program policy and success measures; never treat synthetic balances as program results. |
| Authorized rewards approvers | Approve and audit any points, tier, offer, reward or redemption action through the authorized workflow. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the agent Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, environment access, authenticated audience and data policies before member data is connected. |
| Loyalty data connection owners | Approve read-only ledger, preference and CRM/ERP connections, their identities and consent scope; own access failures. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check CLR-01 through CLR-04 and the boundary tests; reject blank, duplicate and reshoot-required captures as proof. |
| Operations owner | Own session and credit monitoring, support and configuration recovery; route member actions to the authorized workflow. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures are agreed with named owners.
- [ ] The program owner records the current engagement, liability, reward and tier view before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/customer-loyalty-rewards/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve file, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The approved environment and maker access are recorded, and the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available there.
- [ ] Authenticated program-staff access and only the necessary member-data scopes are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/customer-loyalty-rewards/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/customer-loyalty-rewards/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/customer-loyalty-rewards/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/customer-loyalty-rewards/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Customer Loyalty Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_loyalty-rewards-rules-and-safety.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_loyalty-rewards-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: loyalty-dashboard
9. Add skill: points-summary
10. Add skill: reward-recommendations
11. Add skill: tier-analysis
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass CLR-01: Loyalty Program Director
15. Pass CLR-02: CRM Manager
16. Pass CLR-03: Marketing Leader
17. Pass CLR-04: Loyalty Program Director
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: CLR-01, CLR-02, CLR-03, CLR-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The chosen lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, model, inventory and Draft state.
- [ ] If the portable lane is used, the smoke test calls `CustomerLoyaltyRewardsAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged locked prompt passes once in a separate fresh conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Each case passes on the full final response; an annotated screenshot does not replace the machine gate.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before member data is reachable. Request only read scopes for the four informational skills. Restrict the program audience and test authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Approved read-only loyalty ledger

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Loyalty data connection owners

1. **Bind Approved read-only loyalty ledger — read:** Bind approved read-only ledger actions; expose no points adjustment.

2. **Identity for Approved read-only loyalty ledger:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved read-only loyalty ledger:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved read-only loyalty ledger:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Change no points; explain the balance as informational and name the authorized workflow. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Name the authorized workflow, take no action and state that no side effect occurred.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved consented CRM preference feed

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Loyalty data connection owners

1. **Bind Approved consented CRM preference feed — read:** Bind a read-only feed limited to consented preferences.

2. **Identity for Approved consented CRM preference feed:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved consented CRM preference feed:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved consented CRM preference feed:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Contact no member and create no offer; return review-only options. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Name the authorized workflow, take no action and state that no side effect occurred.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Dynamics CRM and ERP through approved read-only integrations

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Loyalty data connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics CRM and ERP through approved read-only integrations — read:** Add approved Dataverse tables as knowledge or bind read-only actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics CRM and ERP through approved read-only integrations:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics CRM and ERP through approved read-only integrations:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics CRM and ERP through approved read-only integrations:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Change no tier; compare thresholds and progress as analysis, not eligibility. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Name the authorized workflow, take no action and state that no side effect occurred.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Authorized rewards workflow

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Loyalty data connection owners

1. **Bind Authorized rewards workflow — write:** Gate an authenticated, audited workflow behind explicit approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Authorized rewards workflow:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Authorized rewards workflow:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Authorized rewards workflow:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Contact no member and create no offer; return review-only options. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Name the authorized workflow, take no action and state that no side effect occurred.

### Step 3-5. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Loyalty data connection owners

Bind only approved read-only connections and keep every write action separate.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved read-only connections preserve the reviewed input and output contract; no balance change is claimed without tool evidence.
- [ ] Any rewards workflow action requires authenticated tools, authorization checks, explicit human approval and audit logging.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test program-staff and unshared identities in an approved test deployment; a maker's access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The program owner sets acceptance measures on customer data; synthetic balances, values and tiers are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; exact assertions stay separate from General quality scoring.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked loyalty corpus | All four cases, CLR-01 through CLR-04, satisfy every required marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| Member-action boundary | Any contact, enrollment, points or tier change, offer, reward, redemption, refund, order or purchase is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoints | Reusable captures show a positive anchor; blank, duplicate and reshoot-required captures are withheld. |
| Release state | The validated manual and pilot agents remain Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Loyalty program owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Loyalty program owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved program audience and channels are configured and tested before publication.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed sessions, unknown-member answers, connection errors and credit use in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, authentication errors and credit consumption after rollout.

## Deliverables Checklist

### Template provides

- [ ] Agent, synthetic data and component inventory.
- [ ] Integration/identity contracts and evaluation cases.
- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Adapted mappings, identities, governance and connections.
- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
